clue.text: The record is less than 500 — under 500

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces before this word sit beneath the piece after it

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
taken as written
C, the Roman numeral for 100, is a figure below 500

explanation.surface: Someone complains a record sold fewer than five hundred copies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts IS and C below D in this down entry. C is 100 in Roman numerals, which is indeed less than 500.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, the flat vinyl kind.

clue.text: City house that's sound

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A building in town that is structurally solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but it is the noun: a reflected noise.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound bounced back off a surface.

clue.text: Minor point to be put to the French

parts.note: les is French for 'the' (plural)
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A small detail is to be raised with the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesser or smaller in importance; minor and less both describe something of smaller degree.

clue.text: Having to turn to a fellow Turk

indicators.note: to turn the first word to is to read it backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Someone has to go over to another Turkish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses the first 'to' to give OT; the second 'to' follows as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottoman Empire was the Turkish state, so an Ottoman is a Turk of that era.

clue.text: Cash and capital articles must be original

parts.note: P, for penny or pence, stands for a small sum of money
Rome is the capital of Italy
the and an are the definite and indefinite articles
the and an are the definite and indefinite articles

explanation.surface: An instruction that money and goods from a capital city must be genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' gives two pieces, THE and AN, the two grammatical articles. 'capital' is a capital city, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Promethean means boldly creative or inventive, after Prometheus who stole fire for mankind.

clue.text: A public school with screen potential

definitions.text: A public school with screen potential

parts.words: A public school with screen potential
parts.note: an old fee-paying English school whose name is shared by a famous rifle and the western film named after it

explanation.surface: A school that might make a good film location.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester College is an ancient English public school (in Britain a public school is a private fee-paying one); Winchester '73 is a Hollywood western.
explanation.definitionFit: The school shares its name with a rifle that gave a classic western film its title.

clue.text: Barker, the revolutionary producer of 9

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
9-across is a crossword, and the person who produces one is a setter

explanation.surface: A rebel who creates puzzles, named Barker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker' looks like a surname but is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog barks, and the Irish red setter is a breed of gundog.

clue.text: Kind and virtuous person without alternative

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the saint goes round the other piece

parts.note: ST, saint, is a virtuous person
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A good person who has no other choice but to be kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not 'lacking'; read it as lacking and the clue makes no sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a type or kind of thing.

clue.text: Owls hatched early in the year make only gradual progress

indicators.note: hatched as in devised or worked up, so the letters of owls are rearranged

parts.note: March is an early month of the year

explanation.surface: Owl chicks born in spring grow up slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hatched' looks like the birds being born, but it is the anagram signal; 'early in the year' is a month, not a season.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow march is a deliberately unhurried military pace, so movement forward is gradual.

clue.text: Diversion responsible for grumpy expression

parts.note: cross means bad-tempered
a word is an expression

explanation.surface: A pastime that causes irritable remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle in the newspaper is a pastime, an amusement to pass time.

clue.text: Note which comes from Columbus, Ohio

indicators.note: the letters come out of the run of words Columbus, Ohio

explanation.surface: A letter sent from a city in Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a letter, but it is the musical note of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Soh is the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale.

clue.text: Units about the queen's business

definitions.meaning: the initials stamped on British official mail, On Her Majesty's Service

explanation.surface: Measures concerning royal affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance is measured in units named after Georg Ohm; official envelopes were marked with the initials of On Her Majesty's Service.

clue.text: Tool that gets noticed

definitions.meaning: a toothed blade for cutting wood
the past tense of see, to notice

explanation.surface: An implement that attracts attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting implement with teeth; also the past tense of see, meaning noticed or spotted.

clue.text: Scale for railway construction workers

parts.note: a scale is a plate on a fish, and track builders use a metal plate of that name to join rails end to end

explanation.surface: A measuring scale used by people building railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' suggests measurement, but it is a fish's scale, i.e. a plate on a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishplate is a metal bar bolted across the joint between two rail lengths.

clue.text: A quite unrepeatable faux pas!

parts.note: unrepeatable suggests rude, but it means a blunder you never get to make again because it kills you

explanation.surface: A social blunder too shocking to repeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unrepeatable' looks like 'too rude to quote'; it means a mistake you cannot make twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly mistake leaves no chance of repeating it.

clue.text: A seaside resort in Malta-so well-organised

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday town on the coast of Malta that is very orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-organised' rearranges IN MALTASO. The resort is in Brittany, not Malta.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint-Malo is a walled port and holiday town on the Brittany coast of France.

clue.text: Game country folk without aspiration

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the rural people surround the letter

parts.note: peasants are rural people
H is the aspirate, the breathed sound

explanation.surface: Rural people with no ambition play a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: PEASANTS round H. 'aspiration' is not ambition but the breathy H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Game birds are wild birds shot for sport, and pheasants are the classic example.

clue.text: A friend from the opposing team

definitions.text: A friend from the opposing team

parts.words: A friend from the opposing team
parts.note: friend is one sense, and in chess the final move by the other side ends your game with this word

explanation.surface: A pal who plays for the rival side.
explanation.walkthrough: Mate means a friend, but in chess it is the checkmate the opposing side inflicts.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal or companion; also checkmate, the winning move delivered by an opponent.

clue.text: A music man colouring

definitions.meaning: Sir John ..., the Victorian composer and organist
a person or thing that dyes or tints

explanation.surface: A musician who also dyes things.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Stainer wrote The Crucifixion and was organist of St Paul's.
explanation.definitionFit: Stainer is the surname of an English composer, and one who dyes wood or cloth is a stainer.

clue.text: Historical rides to broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast as in scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Old journeys to be transmitted on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated in history or legend, as in a storied past.

clue.text: Western sportsman can appear a tricky individual

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west or western
an angler is a fisherman, a sportsman with a rod

explanation.surface: A cowboy hunter may turn out to be a slippery customer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wangler gets things by trickery or scheming.

clue.text: Even the home is of no interest

explanation.surface: Even one's house is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: level, an apartment, dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Level ground is flat, a British apartment is a flat, and a dull performance is flat.

clue.text: Pursuit absorbing acceptable modish creature in the main

indicators.note: the hunt takes in the next letter, which ends up inside it

parts.note: a search is a pursuit or hunt
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Chasing a trendy, respectable creature in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea, an old poetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny echinoderm lives on the seabed, and the main is a poetic word for the ocean.

clue.text: A mechanical device for running water

definitions.meaning: a rotating part that turns circular motion into back-and-forth motion

explanation.surface: A machine part used for a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam is the river at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine part on a rotating shaft, and the river of Cambridge.

clue.text: Duck in some degree a great old bird

indicators.note: the duck goes into the degree

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, O

explanation.surface: A duck that, to some extent, is a large ancient bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird, but it is a zero, O.
explanation.definitionFit: The moa was a giant flightless bird of New Zealand, now extinct.

clue.text: There's not much variation in such singing

indicators.note: only a small part of the word variation is taken, a short run from its middle

explanation.surface: This style of song has little variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not much' takes a small part of 'variation'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera.

clue.text: A nasty experience resulting from arming the rebellious

indicators.note: rebellious as in unruly and disorderly, so the letters break ranks

explanation.surface: Equipping insurgents leads to trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream, or by extension any horrible ordeal.

clue.text: Inexperienced person upsets Tory constituents

indicators.note: upsets as in knocks over, so the letters fall into another order

explanation.surface: A novice annoys Conservative voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' says the letters of 'Tory' are the material shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a beginner or novice.

clue.text: A kiss is what everything turns on

parts.note: X is the symbol for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A kiss is what makes the world go round.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the line about which a body rotates.

clue.text: With little hesitation go hence

parts.note: er is a brief hesitant sound
taken as written

explanation.surface: Without much delay, go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore.

clue.text: The fuss will be over around the beginning of December

indicators.note: the excess word wraps round the first letter of the month

parts.note: too means excessively, over the limit

indicators.note: only the opening letter of December is taken

explanation.surface: The festivities will be finished by early December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like 'finished' but means excessively.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Hangs about to attend to sheep

indicators.note: the hanging word goes round the other piece

parts.note: slings means hangs or suspends
to hear is to attend, as a court hears a case

explanation.surface: A farmer loiters before seeing to his flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attend to sheep' looks like one phrase about care of a flock; 'to' is only a link and 'sheep' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearlings are young sheep shorn once.
